tagline: The bay side of Cape Cod, at the old road's pace.
intro: Route 6A leaves Bourne and keeps to the bay side of Cape Cod for 34 miles, through Sandwich, Barnstable, Yarmouth, Dennis and Brewster to Orleans. Most of it is called the Old King's Highway, and through Barnstable it was the principal road, its villages the town's main centers from the founding in the late 1630s.

Along it stand eight National Register districts, early Cape houses, sea captains' homes and Victorian buildings, with cranberry bogs and bayside marsh between. When trade moved to the villages on Barnstable's south shore in the 1800s, building along the old road slowed down, and so much of what stands is Federal and Greek Revival.

moments.title: Sandwich
moments.text: Settled in 1637, Sandwich took as its motto "after so many shipwrecks, a haven," and from 1825 its glass factory made lead glass known for its color.

moments.title: Old King's Highway Historic District, Barnstable
moments.text: At the 1763 county courthouse here, in September 1774, a crowd pressed county officials to refuse an act of Parliament, and royal control of the county effectively ended.

moments.title: Brewster
moments.text: Called the Sea Captain's Town for its old captains' houses, Brewster keeps the Old Higgins Farm Windmill of 1795 in Drummer Boy Park, right on Route 6A.
